passed.arch: hero-split (texte à gauche, image plein-bleed à droite)

reasons: A has a cohesive modern warm-wood palette and generous whitespace; B uses a busy tiled wood-pattern background that feels cluttered and dated
A establishes clear visual hierarchy with a confident hero statement and large type; B crams a bienvenue paragraph, nav, sidebar, gallery, tariffs table all into one dense boxed layout
A's typography is refined and intentional (serif display + clean sans body); B mixes a decorative script-like heading with generic sans-serif and bold red accents typical of 2000s-era sites
A's imagery/icons (illustrated wood textures, numbered fabrication list, clean photo cards) feel custom and premium; B's icons/photos look like generic clip-art thumbnails
B has clear legacy-web tells that erode trust/modernity: a 'visitor counter' widget, a note about being optimized for 1024x768 resolution, and a bordered box-within-box frame layout

A's CTA and contact sections (gradient dark band, clear form) feel like a modern conversion-focused site; B's flat tariff table and plain footer feel like a static brochure page from over a decade ago
